reader.title: Lynching of Dell Lockhart, "Kid" Coulter and "Slim"
chips: Lynching of any race (not in the anti-Black count)
bases: Three jailed men accused of horse stealing and murder were taken from the jail at Tierra Amarilla by a 'mob' or 'crowd' and lynched (A2, A21, A31).

Every report says the three were 'lynched', and summaries say they were taken from jail 'by a mob' or 'by a crowd' (A2, A21, A31). The pretext was the crimes they were held for and a reported escape plot (A2, A5).

Nearly all reports reprint one Denver Republican special (A2, A5, A12). A later Arizona item with its own details (the 26th, an arrest at Durango) agrees on the triple lynching of two horse thieves and a murderer (A42).

summary.text: The lynching of Dell Lockhart, "Kid" Coulter and "Slim" was the killing of three jailed men by a mob at Tierra Amarilla, reported as in Colorado, in late October 1881.
Lockhart and the man known as Slim were held for horse stealing and Coulter for a murder, and the lynching was attributed to the discovery of Coulter's plan to kill the guard and escape.
A Denver dispatch to the Republican carried the news to papers from Maine to Arizona, where it ran mostly as a one-paragraph item.
According to the Denver dispatch, Lockhart and Slim had been arrested for horse stealing a few weeks before, and Coulter was imprisoned for a murder committed at Chama nine months earlier.
Some versions put the horse-stealing arrests only "a few days ago" or "several weeks ago."
A later item in the Arizona Weekly Citizen said the men had been arrested at Durango, Col., a short time before their deaths.
The three were in the jail at Tierra Amarilla when, in the words of the Savannah Morning News, they were "taken from the jail" and "lynched by a mob."
The Trenton Sentinel said they were "taken out of prison by a crowd," and no report named any member of the mob, gave its size or said where the men were killed.
The dispatch gave the immediate cause as the discovery of Coulter's plan to kill the guard and escape, while the Rock Island Argus version had him planning to kill "the guard and sheriff."
Only the Superior Times, with its reference to "hempen cravats," indicated that the men were hanged.
No report of an inquest, of arrests of the lynchers or of any official response appears in the coverage.

The story reached most papers through a Republican special from Denver, reprinted almost word for word on October 28 and 29 in Washington, Memphis, Rock Island, Carson City, Salt Lake City and Wheeling.

Headlines were brief and factual in most papers, such as "Triple Lynching" in Salt Lake City and "A Trio Lynched" in Somerset, Pa., but the Memphis Public Ledger headed the item "Colorado Amusement" and the Wheeling Register "The Wild Western Way."

Weekly news summaries in Kansas, Mississippi, Montana and New Jersey condensed the dispatch further in early November, and the Lexington, Mo., Intelligencer reduced it to "Three horse thieves were lynched in Colorado last week."

The Superior Times described the lynching in theatrical terms, calling it "an exciting drama" in whose "last act" the three prisoners "made their exit from the world's stage ornamented with hempen cravats."
No paper questioned the charges against the men, whom several items simply called horse thieves and a murderer.
None of the reports stated the race of any of the three men.
The date varies because the same dispatch ran under both October 27 and October 28 Denver datelines with the phrase "last night."

The Evening Star's "Wednesday night," the October 27 datelines and the Arizona Weekly Citizen's "on the 26th" point to October 26, while the Wheeling Register and St. Paul Daily Globe said "Thursday night" and several summaries said "on the 27th."
Nearly every report placed Tierra Amarilla in Colorado, but the Canton, Miss., American Citizen gave it as "N. Mex."
A garbled brief in the Daily Kennebec Journal named only "Nick Coultier, a murderer" and Slim, apparently mistaking Lockhart's name for the dateline.

framing.detail: Most papers ran the Denver wire unchanged as a one-paragraph item, headed 'LYNCHED.', 'Three Men Lynehed.' or 'Triple Lynching.'
Some headlines treated it lightly or as regional color: 'Colorado Amusement' (Memphis) and 'The Wild Western Way' (Wheeling).
The Superior Times called it 'an exciting drama' whose 'last act' left the prisoners 'ornamented with hempen cravats', labeling them horse thieves and a murderer.

conflicts.note: The same Republican special ran under both Oct. 27 and Oct. 28 datelines, so 'last night' yields both dates; the Evening Star's 'Wednesday night' and the Oct. 27 datelines point to October 26.
Almost every report says Colorado; one weekly summary says New Mexico, and another late item notes the men had been arrested at Durango, Col., implying a move from there (A42).
